Mailbox is free software: GPL-3.0-only, copyright wander wildwood for what is written here. It is built on Thunderbird for Android; that and everything else it bundles keeps its own license, each on its own page.

It connects only to the mail servers you enter. Nothing is sent to us, and your address and password stay on this phone. Setting up an account, it also asks the address\'s own domain, and Mozilla\'s list of mail providers, which is told the domain and not the address.

This app is made by wander wildwood, an independent developer: one person, not a company. That makes wander wildwood the data controller for anything the app itself handles, and that is very little: what you put in stays on this phone unless you send it somewhere yourself, or the app sends it to your mail provider and Mozilla\'s autoconfig service as described above, and nothing comes to the developer.
Write to email@wanderthe.dev, about your data or anything else.

Under the GDPR you can ask to see the data held about you, to have it corrected or deleted, to limit or object to its use, to take a copy with you, to withdraw consent, and to complain to a data protection authority. Since the app keeps what it stores only on your phone, you can do most of this yourself: remove an account or delete mail in the app, export your settings to a file, clear the app\'s data in Android\'s settings, or uninstall the app. What your mail provider and Mozilla\'s autoconfig service receive is covered by their own privacy policies.
